description: Decide whether a restructuring PRESERVED FUNCTION. Every divergence between the base and the restructured design is classified function / structure / supporting, and the verdict is `preserved`, `not_preserved` or `indeterminate`. Anything the rules cannot place lands in `unclassified` and forces `indeterminate`; a reworded capability (a rename and a scope change are the same bytes) comes back with both values for a human. It reads two design records and no code, so it never certifies the implementation. On a registry server, give `other_graph_id` instead of a path. Ask for this when you want to know whether a restructuring or reorganisation changed what the system does or only how it is organised — proof that no function was lost.

base_path.description:
Path to the base export document — the design BEFORE the
restructuring. Typically the committed export, or the export at the
commit the restructuring started from. Required unless
`other_graph_id` is passed, which makes the live graph the base.

other_graph_id.description:
The restructured design BY GRAPH_ID, on a server that holds many
designs (a registry behind a trusted host): the live graph is the base,
labelled by this design's graph_id, and the other design is read from
the one the server already holds, inside the set of designs the host
says you may read. Not combined with a path; refused on a single-design
server, and for a design outside that set.

other_path.description:
Path to the restructured document. Omit to certify the live graph —
"did the work in this session move structure without moving function?".

name: certify_preservation
title: Certify Function Preserved
